question: How a standing stone becomes a body.

options.label: A
options.name: Menhir: one weathered slab is body and head, boulder hands and feet
options.question: The standing stone stays one stone: the slab itself stands up, a face carved by weather in its top third and the circle's ring carved on its chest; the limbs are boulders that came with it.
parts: familiar perch: the crown, on the moss cap (S/E/W the same anchor; the slab top is flat enough)
far foot / far fist (stone_cool / stone, a tone back): layer 0; hip / chest; E/W only
fern behind his LEFT ear (grass, two fronds): layer 1 in S and E (behind the slab), 4 in W (over the back of the head); head; sways a frame late on walk and hop
feet x2 (stone_cool boulders): layer 2; hip; 6-frame walk as a slow rock-and-shuffle, 1 px lift
slab (stone, lichen clusters, carved ring, cracks): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px, leans 1 px into the walk; bends only at the foot (hop is a 2 px rise and a dust puff)
face (brow ledge, glowflora eyes in ink sockets, nose ridge, crack mouth): painted on the slab; head; blink = glow off for 140 ms; looks by moving the glow in the socket
moss cap and drips (leaf lobes): layer 4; head; grows a tuft in the fidget
shoulder boulders x2 and fists x2 (stone siblings): layer 5; chest / hand; swing in walk, the fists raise to guard (Bedrock), the shoulder leads the special shoulder charge
options.pose: Upright and patient as the stone he was, hands hanging, face kind; the fidget: a new moss tuft sprouts on his shoulder and he looks down at it, brows up, mouth a small o.
notes: Works: the tallest, plainest silhouette in the cast, a tombstone with a fern, readable in two values at game scale; the slab face says "standing stone" before anything else.
Risk: one slab has no neck or waist, so walk and fight lean on the boulder limbs and 1 px leans; the face must stay in the top third or he reads as a sign post.
Compared with Eastward 05 (John, the heavy-set tallest figure, 3-4 tones a garment) and the mossy rocks of its world shots: lichen as 2-4 px clusters, a lit lip under every crack.

options.label: B
options.name: Cairn stack: piled round stones under a wide capstone brim
options.question: A woken cairn: each body part is a stone set on the one below (feet, hips, belly, chest, head), the capstone on top shades his eyes like a brim, the arms are three pebbles each.
parts: familiar perch: on the capstone (a flat shelf, the best perch in the cast)
far foot and far arm pebbles (a tone back): layer 0; hip / chest; E/W only
fern behind his LEFT ear (grass): layer 1 under the capstone in S/E, 4 in W; head
feet x2 (flat stones): layer 2; hip; 6-frame walk as stepping stones
hip stone, belly stone, chest stone (stone siblings, moss in the joints): layers 3-5; hip / chest; each lags the one below by a frame in walk and hop (a gentle stack wobble), squash 1 px in breath
head stone (stone_warm, glowflora eyes under the brim shadow): layer 6; chest
capstone (stone_cool slab, moss cap, drip): layer 7; head; tilts 1 px in hit and cheer
arm pebbles x3 a side (the last one the fist): layer 6; chest / hand; a chain that swings, the fists close together in guard; the shoulder charge throws the chest stone first
options.pose: Comfortable and heavy, belly stone forward, eyes glowing from under the brim; the fidget: he settles, every stone crunching a little lower, eyes shut, a pebble shaken loose.
notes: Works: the capstone brim gives the cast a second hat shape (no hood, no nightcap) and a hard shadow over the eyes, so the glow reads; the stack shows "built of a place" at once.
Risk: many round parts make a lumpy outline; the stack wobble costs extra rig layers. Close to Tuff in spirit, so Tuff keeps hex columns and stays low and wide.
Compared with Eastward 05: the brim shadow on hats and the curly-haired woman's lobes (each stone a lobe with a lit cap and a dark crescent).

options.label: C
options.name: Moss-mantled giant: broad boulder body, sunk head, long slab arms
options.question: A stone that grew a body: a broad boulder with a smaller head sunk between the shoulders, a thick moss mantle over the shoulders, arms of stacked slabs hanging to the knee.
parts: familiar perch: the near shoulder, in the moss mantle
far hand slab and far leg (a tone back): layer 0; chest / hip; E/W only
fern behind his LEFT ear (grass): layer 1 in S/E, 5 in W; head
legs x2 (stone_cool pillars) and feet (boulders): layer 2; hip; short 6-frame stomp
body boulder (stone, cracks, lichen): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px, sways into the walk
head (stone_warm, brow ledge, glowflora eyes, nose lump): layer 4; chest; sunk, turns 1 px
moss mantle (leaf lobes, drips): layer 5; chest; follows the body a frame late, tuft grows on rest
arms x2: upper, fore and hand slabs (stone siblings): layer 6; chest / hand; long swing, the two hand slabs cross as a wall in guard; the shoulder charge leads with the mantle shoulder
wren (earth, path): fidget prop only, lands on the near hand slab
options.pose: A gentle giant with his shoulders up and arms long, slow and careful; the fidget: a wren lands on his raised palm and he holds very still, eyes on it.
notes: Works: the widest shoulders in the cast and arms that reach the knee give a gentle-giant read; the moss mantle is the most moss of the three and reads at 2 device px.
Risk: the mantle over the shoulders must never close over the head (Nix owns the hood); the head is small, so the face leans on the glow.
Compared with Eastward 05 (John: big shoulders, small head, long arms) for the mass, and the mossy world rocks for the moss lobes over stone.

final.name: Moss-mantled giant (final): broad boulder, capstone brow, ring on the chest
grafts: From A: the circle's ring carved on his chest; its lower groove is a faint glowflora that brightens in a cast (seen edge-on on the front plane in E/W).
From A: the brow set higher; the face now fills the head under the cap (eyes at y 24, not 25-26).
From B: a flat capstone on his head with its hard two-row shadow over the glowing eyes; moss only at its shaded back end with a 2 px drip, never a full cap (Tam's beanie).

E/W rebuilt with depth: the same broad boulder side-on (26 px deep), a side plane, a 4 px front plane split by one hard step (lit facing W, shaded facing E) and a lit shoulder top plane under the moss.
parts: familiar perch: the back shoulder on the moss mantle (E: x smaller, W: x larger); layer 0.5; chest
far arm (upper, fore, hand slabs, a tone back): layer 0; chest / hand; E/W fight poses
far leg (stone_cool pillar, boulder foot, a tone back): layer 1; hip; all facings
near leg (pillar, boulder foot): layer 2; hip; short 6-frame stomp, forward in sit, lifted 2 px in hop
body boulder (stone; side plane plus front plane in E/W; cracks, lichen; the ring rune with a glowflora groove): layer 3; hip; breath 1 px, leans up to 3 px in strike and hit
fern behind his LEFT ear (grass): layer 3.5 (S, E: behind the head), 5.5 in W (over its back); head
head (stone_warm, nose lump, glowflora eyes in ink sockets, mouth line): layer 4; chest; blink = glow off 140 ms, looks by moving the glow
capstone (stone_cool slab, moss at the back end): layer 4.5; head; stays level in every pose
moss mantle (leaf lobes, drips): layer 5; chest; one painter, shifts with the body (no lag frames)

near arm (upper, fore, hand slabs, rotated per pose): layer 6; chest / hand; swing, guard (hand slab up), strike (full reach), cast (raised), cheer (both up); Bedrock shoulder charge leads with the mantle
wren (earth, path): fidget prop only, on the near hand slab
final.pose: A gentle giant, shoulders up and arms long, slow and careful; a wren lands on his palm and he holds still. In a fight he plants and punches with the hand slab; his ring glows when he casts.
notes: Compared side by side with Eastward 05 at the same height: John (broad shoulders, a small head, long arms, 3-4 tones a material), the hard shadow under hat brims, and the mossy world rocks.
Apart from Tuff: Cairn is tall (58 px), grey and matte, upright, with moss and a fern; Tuff stays low, wide, black basalt hex columns, glossy, no moss.
Open: the capstone is the natural perch, but a 24 px familiar on it would leave the 80 px cell (stone top at y 17); it perches on the back shoulder until the familiar size is settled.
Lone pixels and W-E are within the gates in every view; the cheer stays inside the cell.
